tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final configuration on any peg must be a descending stack: larger disks at the bottom and smaller disks above.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When checking whether the goal state is satisfied or when planning to place a disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Goal peg should end as [5,4,3,2,1]; any move that puts 2 below 3 violates this ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In a three‑peg problem, the peg that is neither the source nor the destination can be used as a temporary holding place for disks while larger disks are moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk needs to be moved but its source peg has smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 from peg 1 to peg 2 while disks 1, 3, 4 are temporarily placed on peg 0.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg that is empty or whose top disk is larger; if the destination’s top disk is smaller, it must be moved elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move in the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is 2 is illegal; you must relocate disk 2 first.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to verify that every move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have written the complete move list, before output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Step through the 30 moves in the solution and confirm that peg 2 ends with [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: All peg identifiers in the output must be 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering (e.g., 1‑based) will cause the answer to be rejected.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing each move in the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The move of disk 3 from peg 1 to peg 2 is written as [3,1,2], not [3,2,3].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain an up‑to‑date record of the topmost disk on every peg after each move, so you know which disks are movable and which destinations are legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the construction of the move sequence, after each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 from peg 1 to peg 0, peg 0’s top becomes 1, making disk 2 no longer movable until disk 1 is relocated.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can safely place a smaller disk onto that peg, building the final stack from bottom up.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has some of the larger disks in their final positions.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 on peg 2, disk 4 can be moved onto peg 2 because 5 > 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Smallest Disk as Flexible Buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating ordering, making it an ideal temporary holder to free up larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to clear a peg or move a larger disk but the smallest disk is on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 from peg 1 to peg 0 to expose disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Target Stack from Largest to Smallest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final configuration by placing the largest remaining disk onto the target peg first, then sequentially place the next largest disk on top, ensuring the stack grows in descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When planning the overall sequence; especially useful when the goal is to gather all disks on one peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: First move disk 5 to the goal peg, then disk 4, then disk 3, then disk 2, and finally disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Model may focus on moving the desired disk without checking the destination's top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Model forgets that only the top disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Track the top disk on each peg and only select that disk for a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Model tries to finish quickly without respecting final ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the 'Build Target Stack from Largest to Smallest' strategy or ensure larger disks are already positioned before placing smaller ones.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Model defaults to natural human counting.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Remember that the output format expects peg numbers 0, 1, 2.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Model assumes the constructed sequence is correct without checking.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the move list, simulate the moves (using the 'Simulate Final Configuration' skill) to ensure correctness.
